transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2025-11-19
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 58 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Maya Ortiz (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (KeystoneWare - ML Ops), Tom Reyes (KeystoneWare - VP Eng), Lena Park (KeystoneWare - Security), Ben Ortiz (KeystoneWare - Platform PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be brief):
- KeystoneWare is evaluating a one-year renewal with a capacity uplift to support APAC traffic and is considering a dedicated APAC pool or VPC-hosted option.
- Key concerns: security/compliance integration (KMS/SSO/audit), predictable latency for search/generation endpoints, and cost delta between hosted vs dedicated reserved capacity.
- Next steps: Redwood to send revised quote, schedule security deep-dive, provision APAC test pool for benchmarking.

Topics: renewal pricing, APAC edge test, VPC vs Dedicated, SSO/KMS, benchmarking plan, timeline

Transcript: 
[00:00] Maya Ortiz: Okay, we're live — thanks everyone for joining. Maya from Redwood here, Samir's with me, hmm Samir you want to intro? 
[00:07] Samir Patel: Yeah hi all, Samir Patel, solutions engineer. We'll mostly walk through the technical asks, provisioning, and how we can hit your p95 latency targets in APAC.
[00:15] Aisha Khan: Great, thanks. Quick note, we're on a tight timeline — renewal window is end of month, and product wants APAC availability before end of Q1. So two asks: uplift capacity for peak search traffic and a clear path for APAC private/vpc option.
[00:29] Tom Reyes: And to add, we need predictable token unit math — last quarter cost variance surprised finance. Need a little more guardrails.
[00:37] Maya Ortiz: Understood. Today's goal: agree on a proposal that covers (1) capacity uplift numbers and options (hosted burst vs dedicated APAC pool vs private deployment), (2) security checklist for legal, and (3) concrete next steps to hit your timeline.
[00:49] Lena Park: We'll start with security then; SOC2 and SAML we already have internal docs for, but we need to validate KMS integration and customer-managed keys for APAC. Are those available in Redwood Private or Dedicated?
[01:04] Samir Patel: Short answer: yes, we support customer-managed KMS with Private and with Dedicated via bring-your-own-key for certain tiers. For Hosted API, we have provider-managed keys but there is an enterprise option. We'll go through the exact matrix in the security deep-dive.
[01:19] Ben Ortiz: Can you say more about audit logs? We need immutable access logs that tie to our SSO and to show proof for compliance audits.
[01:26] Samir Patel: We emit per-request audit entries and you can ship them to your SIEM; for Dedicated/Private we can enable longer retention and S3 export. The per-token tracing is limited to sampling by default but we can turn on full tracing in a dedicated pool. It's a cost/size trade-off.
[01:42] Aisha Khan: Perfect. On the capacity side, current usage is top-line ~200k requests/day, peak 650 RPS during US mornings. We estimate APAC will add about 30% of volume but with higher latency sensitivity — p95 target < 200ms for generation endpoints.
[02:00] Tom Reyes: Right, the search feature is latency sensitive, and we saw p99 spikes up to 1.2s during batch backfills. We want to avoid that in APAC.
[02:10] Samir Patel: Given those numbers, we recommended a 4 GPU dedicated APAC pool as a starting point, with autoscale for burst up to 6. That should yield expected p95 into ~120-180ms for the shorter prompts; long-form generation might be 250ms-plus depending on sequence length and model.
[02:30] Maya Ortiz: Financial note — for the 4 GPU pool reserved for 12 months, we've run rough math. Long-term committed price vs pay-as-you-go hosted shows about 30% cost savings at your current volume if you commit. But there is a setup delta for Private (one-time infra fee).
[02:45] Tom Reyes: Can you put numbers on that? Finance will want a line-item.
[02:48] Maya Ortiz: Yes, we'll include a delta sheet. Example: reserved 4xA40-class-equivalent pool vs hosted usage at current token assumptions — I'll send a detailed appendix.
[02:59] Lena Park: Also, how does KV cache or prefix caching work with multi-region? If we serve APAC from a different cluster, cold KV misses might be higher.
[03:09] Samir Patel: Good call — KV cache is local to the serving pool. For geo-reads we recommend active-active routing with prefix-aware caching: you can pin user cohorts to APAC cluster so their caches are warm. There's also a hybrid approach where we replicate a subset of KV keys for cross-region reads — that adds some complexity.
[03:28] Ben Ortiz: Replication latency concerns me. Is there any out-of-the-box solution in Redwood to replicate KV keys?
[03:33] Samir Patel: We have a replication tool in the ops toolkit for hot keys; it's not a full global KV store but it handles the hot-path prefixes for low-latency retrieval. We'll put that in the runbook.
[03:42] Aisha Khan: Back to timeline — if we sign the renewal by 11/30, can APAC pool be live in staging by mid-January?
[03:50] Samir Patel: Yes, realistic. Provisioning a dedicated pool and routing takes 3-4 weeks with the staging runbook; add a week for canary and traffic shift. For Private on-prem it's longer.
[04:02] Tom Reyes: Let's talk about fallback policies; if APAC pool is saturated, will traffic route back to US? We need graceful degradation.
[04:09] Samir Patel: We support smart routing policies. You can set policy tiers: APAC primary, fallback to US-hosted for best-effort. There's also automatic variant fallback to smaller model for latency-critical endpoints.
[04:21] Maya Ortiz: Quick pause — does anyone have a question on pricing models? I know finance asked about unit economics and predictability.
[04:28] Tom Reyes: We want a cap or alerting if cost deviates more than 10% month-over-month. Is there a way to set hard limits?
[04:35] Maya Ortiz: You can set quotas and alerts at token-level; hard stop is possible for hosted tiers, less so for dedicated pools unless you instrument burst caps. We'll outline guardrails in the quote.
[04:46] Lena Park: On encryption: can Redwood integrate with our HSM/CloudKMS in APAC region? Our auditors require keys never to leave the region.
[04:55] Samir Patel: For Private deployments yes — HSM integration is supported and keys remain in-region. For Dedicated in our managed region, we can BYOK with a customer KMS instance located in APAC depending on provider constraints. We'll confirm region-level key residency in the security deep-dive.
[05:12] Aisha Khan: One more technical — model quantization/throughput. We currently run an open Llama variant for embeddings+rerank. Do you recommend quantizing for APAC dedicated pool?
[05:21] Samir Patel: Yes, quantization profiles can reduce memory and increase throughput. We'll recommend a q4_0 profile for embeddings and a mixed-int8 path for generation. We'll share benchmarks vs your sample traffic.
[05:33] Ben Ortiz: Do you support A/B rollouts for model versions during a migration? We want canary small percent traffic to new APAC pool.
[05:39] Samir Patel: Absolutely — rollouts are supported with traffic splits and automatic rollback on quality regressions. You can tie regressions to prompt-based evals.
[05:48] Tom Reyes: Competitor question — we're also looking at CloudAI which claimed simpler APAC routing. What's Redwood's differentiation here?
[05:55] Maya Ortiz: Short answer: production-grade controls (deterministic SLOs, KV cache controls, and actionable cost levers). We'll send a short competitive sheet that maps features.
[06:06] Aisha Khan: Okay, let's capture explicit numbers for the quote: baseline reserved 4 GPU pool in APAC with autoscale to 6, 12-month term, 99.5% uptime SLA, sampling audit logs with option to enable full tracing for dedicated pool. Include option B: hosted + burst (no dedicated) for 6 months to test.
[06:27] Maya Ortiz: Noted. Samir, can you confirm what we need from KeystoneWare to run the APAC latency benchmark next week?
[06:33] Samir Patel: We'll need a 48-hour representative traffic dump with timestamps, distribution by prompt length, and a list of the top 100 hot keys for KV replication. Also credentials for a staging SSO test user and a test dataset.
[06:47] Ben Ortiz: We'll export that and hit your secure upload.
[06:50] Lena Park: On the legal side, what's the contract amendment process? Can we get a redline in 5 business days?
[06:56] Maya Ortiz: Yes, our legal team will produce an amendment once we agree on scope; I can get a draft to you within 5 business days after sign-off on pricing.
[07:05] Tom Reyes: A couple of quick clarifying comments — when you say reserved 4 GPUs, what GPU class is that? A40, H100? We need to correlate model performance.
[07:13] Samir Patel: For the example pricing we assumed A40-equivalent. If you prefer H100-class we can price that but it'll change cost and density assumptions — we'll include options.
[07:23] Aisha Khan: How are burst hours billed? If we autoscale to 6 GPUs for 3 hours, is it prorated hourly or daily?
[07:30] Maya Ortiz: Prorated hourly for dedicated with reserved baseline; hosted burst is per-token. We'll detail the hourly prorate in the quote.
[07:39] Ben Ortiz: Any known gotchas for routing mobile clients in APAC? We have a lot of mobile-only users.
[07:44] Samir Patel: Mobile clients are fine; we recommend edge pre-warming and a CDN front for static assets. Model inference still hits the cluster; avoid synchronous long-form generation on mobile.
[07:55] Aisha Khan: One more ask — can Redwood provide a short runbook for incident response: who to page for latency, who to page for security?
[08:01] Maya Ortiz: Yes, we'll include on-call contacts and escalation paths in the ops appendix.
[08:06] Tom Reyes: Great.
[08:08] (cross-talk)
[08:10] Maya Ortiz: Summarizing next steps: Maya will send pricing + delta; Samir will spin up a test bench and run initial APAC latency tests once we have traffic profile; Lena will coordinate security docs; Ben will send usage exports. We sketch the timeline for staging mid-Jan if we execute now.
[08:26] Aisha Khan: That works. I just want to call out one risk — if the APAC providers have capacity shortages in Q1 we might see delayed provisioning. How does that affect SLAs?
[08:36] Samir Patel: We have capacity buffers and partner agreements; however, if on-prem or specific instance types are scarce we may propose HOD alternatives or model-tier fallback for the temporary period. We'll surface this in the SOW.
[08:49] Tom Reyes: Okay, last thing — can you also include an addendum around data residency and deletion policy? Legal will want that spelled out.
[08:57] Lena Park: Yes, and retention windows for logs.
[09:01] Maya Ortiz: We'll include both. Anything else?
[09:04] Ben Ortiz: No, that's all from my side.
[09:06] Aisha Khan: Thanks, appreciate the detail. We'll target internal alignment tomorrow and get you the exports.
[09:12] Maya Ortiz: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the quote and calendar invites for security deep-dive and the provisioning kickoff.

(End of call — 15:58 PST)
